ISSUES 3.

Vide order dated 28/11/2023, the following issues were framed by this Tribunal :-
1.

Whether the deceased Mohd. Farman suffered fatal injuries in an accident that took place on 10.07.2022 at about 12.05 AM involving vehicle bearing registration No. DL-2SP-3682 driven by the Respondent No. 1 rashly and negligently and owned by the Respondent No.2?

OPP.
2.
Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation?

If so, to what amount and from whom?
3.Relief.

I have perused the record and my issue wise findings are as under:-
" Whether the deceased Mohd. Farman suffered fatal injuries in an accident that took place on 10.07.2022 at about 12.05 AM involving vehicle bearing registration No.
DL-2SP-3682 driven by the Respondent No. 1 rashly and negligently and owned by the Respondent No.2? OPP.''
8.

It is well settled that the procedure followed for proceedings conducted by an accident tribunal is similar to that followed by a civil court and in civil matters the facts are required to be established by preponderance of probabilities only and not by strict rules of evidence or beyond reasonable doubts as are required in a criminal prosecution.

The burden of proof in a civil case is never as heavy as that is required in a criminal case, but in a claim petition under the Motor Vehicles Act, this burden is infact even lesser than that in a civil case.

Reference in this regard can be made to the propositions of law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Bimla Devi and others Vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, reported in (2009) 13 SC 530, which were reiterated in the subsequent judgment in the case of Parmeshwari Vs. Amir Chand and others 2011 (1) SCR 1096 Salma Lrs Of Deceased (F)(Fir 357/2022/ ... vs Nameer Hasan S/O. Alam Hasan on 15 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/80191665/
5 (Civil Appeal No.1082 of 2011) and also recently in another case Mangla Ram Vs. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. & Ors., 2018 Law Suit (SC) 303.

In order to prove the present issue, the petitioners has examined PW-2 Sh. Sameer @
Sameeruddin (eye witness). PW-2 deposed during the course of present enquiry that the at the relevant date, time and place, he was sitting at the Rikshaw Garrage of his father and he had seen that the deceased Farman was going to bring a Rikshaw from Gali Gurdware Wali and when he reached at the Shardhanand Marg Road (S.N.Marg Road) all of sudden the Scooty bearing registration no. DL-2SP-3682 came from Lahori Gate Chowk, Delhi which was being driven by the R-1 in a very rash and negligent and zig zag manner, without caring fro the traffic rules and padesterians and without blowing any horn, hit the deceased and due to the said impact the deceased Farman Fell on the road and sustained various serious injuries.

He further deposed that the driver of the Scooty was also fell down on the road with Scooty and the impact of the Scooty with the deceased was such a forceful that some parts of the Scooty including its front number plate were broken and were fell on the road.

He further deposed that the driver of the Scooty was apprehended by him and when he tried to take Farman in a Rikshaw so that he may be taken to hospital at this moment the driver of Scooty fled from the spot alongwith Scooty and the driver of the Scooty was later on arrested by the police was correctly identified by him.

He further deposed that the accident had occurred due to the rash, zig-zag and negligent and speedily driving on the part of the driver of the Scooty who was driving the offending vehicle so rashly and MACT No. 892/22 Salma Vs.

examined by the respondents
In totality, the testimony of PW-2 seems reliable and worth acting upon.
Since, PW-2 has categorically stated that the deceased Mohd. Farman died as driver of the offending vehicle hit his Scooty to the deceased.

10. It is not denied that R-1 was charge-sheeted for the offences punishable under Sections 279/304A IPC & 3/181 & 146/196 MV Act in the above FIR, which in itself is a strong circumstance to support the above oral testimony of PW-1 and the case of petitioners on this issue.

The copies of FIR, charge-sheet, site plan, Mechanical Inspection Report of the offending vehicle, Postmortem Report of deceased, Seizure Memo and Arrest Memo of respondent also corroborate the testimony of PW-1.
11.

Besides the above, R-1 himself was the best witness who could have stepped into the witness box to challenge the deposition being made by PW2 regarding the above accident and its manner etc.,
but he has not done so.

Therefore, an adverse inference on this aspect is also required to be drawn against the respondents in view of the law laid down in case of Cholamandalam M.S. General Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Kamlesh, reported in 2009 (3) AD (Delhi) 310.
12.

sentences.text: Having ruled so, this Tribunal now proceeds to assess the wrongful act, neglect or default of respondent, if any, in driving the offending vehicle at the relevant time.
Admittedly, Respondent has not explained the circumstances under which the accident took place due to his rash and negligent driving.

In the absence of any evidence regarding any mechanical defect in the offending vehicle or any material depicting any negligent/sudden act or omission on the part of the deceased, the only inference possible in the given facts and circumstances is that of neglect and default on the part of respondent while driving the offending vehicle at the relevant time.

In view of the above discussion,
this Tribunal is constrained to hold respondent guilty of gross neglect and default in driving the offending vehicle at the relevant time.

14. In view of the postmortem report pertaining to the deceased placed on record by the petitioners,
no dispute is left regarding the death of the deceased on account of injuries sustained by him in the above accident.
15. In view of the above discussion, this Tribunal holds that the deceased lost his life on account of neglect and default of respondent while driving the offending vehicle at the relevant time.
This issue thus stands decided against the respondent and in favour of the petitioners.

16. As this Tribunal has already held that respondent was responsible for the death of the deceased due to his neglect and default in driving the offending vehicle at the relevant time, therefore, the petitioners have become entitled to be compensated for death of deceased in the above accident, but computation of compensation and liability to pay the same are required to be decided.
COMPENSATION 17.

The compensation to which the petitioners are entitled shall be under the following heads:-
(i) LOSS OF DEPENDENCY 18.
In this regard, the petitioners have examined Petitioner No. 1 as PW1 who was the mother of deceased.
PW-1 deposed that at the relevant time, the deceased was 18 years old and was doing the work of Bawarchi and was earning Rs.20,000/ per month.
However, there is no material available on record which could corroborate the claim of PW-1 as to the monthly earnings of the deceased.

In the facts and circumstances, it would be appropriate to assess the monthly income of the deceased as per the minimum wages payable MACT No. 892/22 Salma Vs. Nameer Hasan & Ors Pages No.

19. Petitioner has claimed that the deceased was aged about 18 years at the time of his death.
She has also placed on record a copy of Aadhar Card of the deceased Ex.PW-1/2.
As per which the year of birth of deceased was 2003.
The date of accident is 10/07/2022.
Going by the Aadhar Card of the deceased, the age of deceased would be around 19 years as on the date of accident.

Hence, in view of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Sarla Verma & Ors. Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr., (2009) 6 SCC 121, which has also been upheld by the Constitutional Bench of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of National Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi & Ors.
SLP (Civil) No. 25590 of 2014, decided on 31.10.2017, the multiplier of '18' is held applicable for calculating the loss of dependency caused to the petitioners on account of death of the deceased.
20. Coming to the dependency of deceased at the time of accident, it may be observed that the deceased is survived by his mother who is considered to be dependent upon the deceased.
21.

RELEASE 26.

26.1 Out of the awarded amount, Petitioner is awarded a sum of Rs.26,00,000/- (Rupees Twenty Six Lakhs Only) and the said amount is directed to be kept with State Bank of India, Branch Tis Hazari Courts, New Delhi in MACAD in the form of 130 monthly fixed deposit receipts (FDRs) payable in equal amounts for a period of 1 to 130 months in succession, as per the scheme formulated by Central Motor Vehicles (fifth Amendment) Rules, 2022 [(Directions at serial no. 35, 36 of Procedure for Investigation of Motor Vehicle Accidents (under Rule 150A)].

The remaining amount of Rs.2,54,876/- (Rupees Two Lakhs Fifty Four Thousand Eight Hundred Seventy Six Only) is also directed to be released into her above said account, which can be withdrawn and utilized by the Petitioner.

27. The Bank(s) shall not permit any joint name(s) to be added in the savings bank account or fixed deposit accounts of the petitioner(s) i.e. the savings bank account(s) of the petitioner(s) shall be an individual savings bank account(s) and not a joint account(s).
The original fixed deposit shall be retained by the SBI, Branch Tis Hazari Courts, Delhi in safe custody.
However, the statement containing FDR number, FDR amount, date of maturity and maturity amount shall be furnished by the bank to the petitioner(s).
The maturity amounts of the FDR(s) be credit by Electronic Clearing System (ECS) in the savings bank account of the petitioner(s) near the place of their residence.
No loan, advance, withdrawal or pre-mature discharge be allowed on the fixed deposits without permission of this Tribunal.

LIABILITY 28. R-1 being the driver and principal tortfeasor and R-2 being owner of the said vehicle, and also being vicariously liable for the acts of R-1, are jointly and severally liable to pay the awarded amount of compensation to petitioner.

opennyai_summary.facts:
Farman S/o Sh. Jamaluddin (hereinafter referred to as "deceased") sustained fatal injuries.
As per petitioner, on 9/10.07.2022 at 11.30 P.M. the deceased Farman was going to bring a Rikshaw from Gali Gurdware Wali and when he reached the Shardhanand Marg Road then all of a sudden the Scooty bearing registration no. DL 2SP 3682(hereinafter referred to as "offending vehicle") came from Lahori Gate Chowk, Delhi, which was being driven by the R1 in a very rash, negligent and zig zag manner, without caring for the traffic rules and padesterians and without blowing any horn, hit the deceased and due to said impact the deceased Farman fell on the road and sustained various serious injuries and the R1 also fell down on road alongwith theScooty at a considerably distance.
DAR was treated as a claim petition.
opennyai_summary.issue:
Whether the deceased Mohd. Farman suffered fatal injuries in an accident that took place on 10.07.2022 at about 12.05 AM involving vehicle bearing registration No. DL-2SP-3682 driven by the Respondent No. 1 rashly and negligently and owned by the Respondent No.2?
Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation?
If so, to what amount and from whom?
3.Relief.
I have perused the record and my issue wise findings are as under:-
" Whether the deceased Mohd. Farman suffered fatal injuries in an accident that took place on 10.07.2022 at about 12.05 AM involving vehicle bearing registration No.
DL-2SP-3682 driven by the Respondent No. 1 rashly and negligently and owned by the Respondent No.2? OPP.''
8.
"Whether the petitioners are entitled to any compensation, if so, to what amount and from whom?"
16. As this Tribunal has already held that respondent was responsible for the death of the deceased due to his neglect and default in driving the offending vehicle at the relevant time, therefore, the petitioners have become entitled to be compensated for death of deceased in the above accident, but computation of compensation and liability to pay the same are required to be decided.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
It is well settled that the procedure followed for proceedings conducted by an accident tribunal is similar to that followed by a civil court and in civil matters the facts are required to be established by preponderance of probabilities only and not by strict rules of evidence or beyond reasonable doubts as are required in a criminal prosecution.
The burden of proof in a civil case is never as heavy as that is required in a criminal case, but in a claim petition under the Motor Vehicles Act, this burden is infact even lesser than that in a civil case.
Reference in this regard can be made to the propositions of law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Bimla Devi and others Vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, reported in (2009) 13 SC 530, which were reiterated in the subsequent judgment in the case of Parmeshwari Vs. Amir Chand and others 2011 (1) SCR 1096 Salma Lrs Of Deceased (F)(Fir 357/2022/ ... vs Nameer Hasan S/O. Alam Hasan on 15 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/80191665/
5 (Civil Appeal No.1082 of 2011) and also recently in another case Mangla Ram Vs. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. & Ors., 2018 Law Suit (SC) 303.
Since, PW-2 has categorically stated that the deceased Mohd. Farman died as driver of the offending vehicle hit his Scooty to the deceased.
Therefore, an adverse inference on this aspect is also required to be drawn against the respondents in view of the law laid down in case of Cholamandalam M.S. General Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Kamlesh, reported in 2009 (3) AD (Delhi) 310.
12.
In view of the above, it could be safely assumed that at the relevant time the deceased had died due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle being driven by respondent.
Having ruled so, this Tribunal now proceeds to assess the wrongful act, neglect or default of respondent, if any, in driving the offending vehicle at the relevant time.
Admittedly, Respondent has not explained the circumstances under which the accident took place due to his rash and negligent driving.
In the absence of any evidence regarding any mechanical defect in the offending vehicle or any material depicting any negligent/sudden act or omission on the part of the deceased, the only inference possible in the given facts and circumstances is that of neglect and default on the part of respondent while driving the offending vehicle at the relevant time.
In view of the above discussion,
this Tribunal is constrained to hold respondent guilty of gross neglect and default in driving the offending vehicle at the relevant time.
15. In view of the above discussion, this Tribunal holds that the deceased lost his life on account of neglect and default of respondent while driving the offending vehicle at the relevant time.
However, there is no material available on record which could corroborate the claim of PW-1 as to the monthly earnings of the deceased.
In the facts and circumstances, it would be appropriate to assess the monthly income of the deceased as per the minimum wages payable MACT No. 892/22 Salma Vs. Nameer Hasan & Ors Pages No.
12/23
Hence, in view of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Sarla Verma & Ors. Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr., (2009) 6 SCC 121, which has also been upheld by the Constitutional Bench of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of National Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi & Ors.
SLP (Civil) No. 25590 of 2014, decided on 31.10.2017, the multiplier of '18' is held applicable for calculating the loss of dependency caused to the petitioners on account of death of the deceased.
20. Coming to the dependency of deceased at the time of accident, it may be observed that the deceased is survived by his mother who is considered to be dependent upon the deceased.
21.
Further, in view of subsequent judgments of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of United India Insurance Company Ltd Vs Satinder Kaur & Ors MANU/HC/0500/2020 and The New India Assurance Company Ltd & Ors Vs Somwati & Ors MANU/HC/0674/2020, the petitioners are also entitled to compensation under the head "loss of consortium": -
Filial Consortium : Rs.44,000/- (Rs. 44,000/- X 1)
24.
opennyai_summary.decision:
This issue thus stands decided against the respondent and in favour of the petitioners.
Irrespective of this, one half of the earnings of deceased shall be deducted towards his personal and living expenses in view of the law already discussed above.
(Supra), the petitioners are also held entitled to an addition of 40% of the above amount of his earnings towards future prospects.
22. Thus, the loss of dependency qua the deceased in the present case comes to Rs.24,95,707/-
(rounded off) (Rs.16,506/- X 140/100 X 1/2 X 12X 18).
This amount is awarded to the petitioners under this head.
(ii) COMPENSATION UNDER NON-PECUNIARY HEADS 23.
In terms of propositions laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Rajwati @ Rajjo & Ors. Vs. United India Insurance Co. Ltd., Civil Appeal No. 8179/2022 decided on 09/12/2022, the petitioners are also held entitled to amounts of Rs. 20,000/- each under the heads of loss of estate and funeral expenses.
Hence, the Petitioners are awarded a total sum of Rs.84,000/- (Rs.20,000/- + 20,000/- + Rs.
44,000/-) under this head.
The Petitioners are thus awarded a sum of Rs. 25,79,707/- (Rupees Twenty Five Lakhs Seventy Nine Thousand Seven Hundred Seven Only) (Rs.24,95,707/- + Rs.84,000/-) along with interest @
8% per annum from the date of filing of DAR i.e. 14/11/2022.
Since no interim compensation has been awarded, therefore no deduction is applicable.
Petitioner did not bother to appear before this Tribunal for recording her statement regarding financial needs and requirements.

The original fixed deposit shall be retained by the SBI, Branch Tis Hazari Courts, Delhi in safe custody.

Hence, the Petitioners are awarded a total sum of Rs.84,000/- (Rs.20,000/- + 20,000/- + Rs.
44,000/-) under this head.
